papers.title: Differential evolution of neuroinflammatory remodeling programs related to scar formation and regeneration in spinal cord injury: A cross-species multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury in mammals often transitions from an acute inflammatory response to persistent neuroinflammatory and scar-associated remodeling, whereas zebrafish attenuate injury-induced inflammatory programs during regenerative repair. The molecular programs underlying these divergent outcomes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated phase-aligned mouse and zebrafish spinal cord injury datasets using single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, pathway and regulon analyses, expression-based ligand-receptor co-expression analysis, machine-lea
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell, single-nucleus, and spatial transcriptomics from mouse and zebrafish spinal cord injury models to compare how neuroinflammatory and scar-associated remodeling programs diverge across species. Using pathway, regulon, ligand-receptor, and machine-learning analyses, the authors identify molecular programs that distinguish persistent mammalian scarring from zebrafish regenerative repair. The work highlights candidate regulators and cell-cell communication axes underlying these divergent injury outcomes.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA Sequencing Analysis Reveals That Targeting PLG-PLGRKT Signaling-mediated Pro-fibrotic Scar-associated Macrophages Ameliorates Liver Fibrosis in Biliary Atresia.
papers.abstract: Biliary atresia (BA) is a severe pediatric cholangiopathy characterized by rapidly progressive liver fibrosis. This study aimed to characterize scar-associated macrophages and investigate the role of plasminogen (PLG)-plasminogen receptor with a C-terminal lysine (PLGRKT) signaling in BA-associated fibrogenesis.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and translational hepatology
papers.summary: Using single-cell RNA sequencing, the authors identified a population of pro-fibrotic scar-associated macrophages in the livers of children with biliary atresia, a pediatric bile duct disease that causes rapid liver scarring. They found that signaling between plasminogen (PLG) and its receptor PLGRKT drives the fibrotic behavior of these macrophages, and that blocking this pathway reduced liver fibrosis in experimental models. This suggests PLG-PLGRKT signaling as a potential therapeutic target for biliary atresia-associated liver disease.

papers.title: Decoding spatial mTOR signalling reveals distinct roles in the tumour microenvironment.
papers.abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprises a variety of cell types that interact with malignant cells, influencing both cancer progression and the patient response to therapy. Given the intricate interactions among these components, assessing how signalling pathways contribute to cancer progression by acting on different components of the TME is particularly complex. Multiplexed imaging allows simultaneous assessment of signalling in multiple of these components. Here, we utilise a highly multiplexed dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to investigate how complex mTOR signalling in d
papers.summary: This study used highly multiplexed imaging of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to map mTOR signalling activity within different cell types of the tumour microenvironment. The analysis reveals that mTOR signalling plays distinct, cell-type-specific roles in the TME, linking pathway activity in specific compartments to cancer progression and potentially therapy response. The work demonstrates how spatial multiplexed profiling can disentangle complex signalling interactions across heterogeneous tissue components.

papers.title: Lossless compression of protein databases for efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification with Centrifuger.
papers.abstract: We present a lossless compression algorithm for indexing a protein database while supporting fast taxonomic classification in the method Centrifuger. The algorithm is a new scheme of the previously proposed run-block compression algorithm to reduce the size of the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index, and it scales better with alphabet size than the original. On the RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, Centrifuger reduces the memory footprint by over a third compared to the method Kaiju that builds on a plain FM-index, while having comparable running time. Furthermore, the compressed FM-ind
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Centrifuger introduces a lossless compression algorithm for protein database indexes that shrinks the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index using a new run-block compression scheme that scales better with alphabet size. On RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, it reduces memory footprint by over a third compared to Kaiju while maintaining comparable running time, enabling efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification.

papers.title: Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr.
papers.abstract: Changes in cell type composition play an important role in human health and disease. Recent advances in single-cell technology have enabled the measurement of cell type composition at increasing cell lineage resolution across large cohorts of individuals. Yet this raises new challenges for statistical analysis of these compositional data to identify changes in cell type frequency. We introduce crumblr ( DiseaseNeurogenomics.github.io/crumblr ), a scalable statistical method for analyzing count ratio data using precision-weighted linear mixed models incorporating random effects for complex stud
papers.summary: The authors present crumblr, a scalable statistical method for analyzing changes in cell type composition from single-cell data. It uses precision-weighted linear mixed models with random effects to handle complex study designs and count ratio data. This provides a flexible tool for identifying shifts in cell type frequency across large cohorts.

papers.title: Variation in enhancer activity across brain regions defines neurological disease risk and shapes cellular pathology.
papers.abstract: Genetic variants associated with neurological traits are enriched in enhancers active in neurons. However, there are many types of neurons with varying functions across the brain, making it difficult to pinpoint insights into disease pathology. We set out to investigate whether cell type and brain region specificity of transcriptional enhancers could reveal new insights into the cellular pathology of neurological traits.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates whether enhancers active in specific brain regions and neuron types can help explain the genetic basis of neurological diseases. The authors find that variation in enhancer activity across brain regions defines neurological disease risk and shapes cellular pathology, suggesting region- and cell-type-specific enhancer maps can pinpoint disease-relevant mechanisms.

papers.title: Gravlax: an annotation-independent molecular evidence archive for single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: A cell-by-gene count matrix is the artifact of a single-cell RNA-seq experiment that is most often stored, shared, and reanalyzed. It is the output of a computation whose inputs are the sequenced molecules and a gene annotation, and while the molecules never change, the annotation is revised continually. Once the matrix has been produced, the evidence behind it can no longer be reinterpreted. Recovering that evidence means returning to raw reads or alignments that are large, costly to process, and frequently unavailable. We ask whether a concise representation of the molecules themselves can b
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Gravlax introduces an annotation-independent archive that stores molecular evidence from single-cell RNA-seq experiments in a compact form, rather than relying on the gene-by-cell count matrix that depends on a specific gene annotation. This allows the underlying evidence to be reinterpreted as annotations are revised, without needing to reprocess large raw reads or alignments. The approach addresses the loss of information when count matrices are shared without the original molecular evidence.

papers.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
papers.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug se
papers.summary: The authors present CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq data into cell-type composition and cell-type-specific expression, then maps these to drug sensitivity. This enables drug response to be resolved at the level of individual cell types within heterogeneous tissue samples.

papers.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
papers.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. Existing supervised approaches rely on accurate reference data, which are lacking for many cancer types, whereas unsupervised
papers.summary: CDState is a computational method that deconvolves bulk tumor RNA sequencing data to resolve intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity into distinct malignant cell states without requiring supervised reference data. This addresses a key limitation of existing approaches that depend on accurate single-cell references, which are unavailable for many cancer types. The method enables scalable characterization of cell-state diversity across large cancer cohorts.

papers.title: Donor-aware integration of public single-cell and spatial transcriptomes identifies a VIC remodeling program and FN1-NT5E spatial association in calcific aortic valve disease.
papers.abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) involves interacting endothelial, interstitial, immune and extracellular-matrix programs, but public single-cell studies contain many cells and few donors. A staged, donor-aware computational workflow was applied to five public human transcriptomic datasets. GSE220774 was used for single-cell discovery; GSE51472, GSE194180 and GSE235995 for fixed-signature replication; and GSE306288 for donor-level spatial assessment. Donors or patients, rather than cells or spots, were treated as biological replicates. VIC9 ranked highest for a prespecified fibrocalcific c
papers.summary: This study applies a donor-aware computational workflow to five public human transcriptomic datasets to study calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD), treating donors rather than individual cells or spots as biological replicates to avoid pseudoreplication. The analysis identifies a valvular interstitial cell (VIC) remodeling program (VIC9) and a spatial association between FN1 and NT5E in CAVD tissue. The work highlights the importance of donor-level replication in integrating public single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartme
papers.summary: Using Visium spatial transcriptomics on lung samples from fatal COVID-19 and control cases, the authors mapped how cell populations and gene expression change across progressive stages of diffuse alveolar damage. They found a progressive loss of endothelial cells, type I pneumocytes, and natural killer cells, alongside an increase in myeloid and stromal cells, particularly peribronchial fibroblasts. Spatial analysis also revealed distinct tissue compartments associated with disease progression.

papers.title: Cellular scaling laws in the mammalian brain.
papers.abstract: Recent whole-brain cell atlases have uncovered a consistent cytoarchitectural feature: the greatest diversity of discrete neuronal cell types resides not in the regions with the most neurons (e.g., the cortex and cerebellum) but rather in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. We propose that this discrepancy reflects a fundamental algorithmic division in the vertebrate brain between a "learning subsystem" and a "steering subsystem." The learning subsystem (cortex, striatum, and cerebellum) scales via the replication of repetitive modules to maximize computational ca
papers.summary: The paper proposes that whole-brain cell atlases reveal a surprising pattern: the regions with the most neurons (cortex, cerebellum) have fewer distinct neuronal cell types than deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. The authors interpret this as evidence for two functionally distinct subsystems in the vertebrate brain—a "learning subsystem" that scales by replicating repetitive modules, and a "steering subsystem" with greater cell-type diversity—suggesting a fundamental algorithmic division of labor.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal a DLL4-associated tip-like endothelial niche linked to neoadjuvant chemotherapy non-response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy non-response remains a major challenge in bladder cancer, yet the endothelial states and intercellular communication programs associated with treatment failure remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic data, computational analyses, and in vitro experiments to characterize endothelial programs associated with chemotherapy response. A non-response-related transcriptional program was preferentially enriched in endothelial cells and was most prominent in the TipEC_2 tip-like endothelial subset. Integrative an
papers.summary: This study integrated single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk transcriptomic data to characterize endothelial cell states associated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy non-response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer. The authors identified a tip-like endothelial subset (TipEC_2) enriched for a non-response transcriptional program and linked to DLL4-associated signaling, suggesting that this endothelial niche contributes to treatment failure. In vitro experiments supported the computational findings.

papers.title: Intranasal HSV‑1 infection drives region‑specific interferon‑dominant microglial remodeling.
papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) is a neurotropic pathogen capable of invading the central nervous system (CNS) and is associated with chronic neuroinflammation, cognitive impairment, and neurodegenerative disease. While microglia orchestrate the initial immune response to HSV‑1, the molecular mechanisms that regulate their sustained neuroinflammatory activity in vivo remain poorly understood. To define the transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms that shape microglial responses during acute HSV-1 infection in vivo, we have, for the first time, integrated single‑nucleus RNA sequencing, chr
papers.summary: This study used single-nucleus RNA sequencing and chromatin accessibility profiling to map how microglia in different brain regions respond to intranasal HSV-1 infection. The authors found that microglia undergo region-specific remodeling dominated by interferon signaling, revealing transcriptional and epigenetic programs that sustain neuroinflammation during acute infection. This provides a resource for understanding how viral infection may contribute to chronic neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Single-cell spatial transcriptomics identifies SERPINE1 as a vascular endothelial mediator of cisplatin resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin resistance remains a major obstacle in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), yet the contribution of the vascular microenvironment and its variation across HPV statuses remains unclear.
papers.summary: Using single-cell spatial transcriptomics, this study maps the vascular microenvironment in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and identifies SERPINE1 in endothelial cells as a mediator of cisplatin resistance, with variation across HPV status. The work highlights how stromal-vascular crosstalk contributes to chemoresistance and nominates SERPINE1 as a potential target.

papers.title: Cell-resolved spatial mapping of antibody-drug conjugate targets in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) activity and target-dependent on-target/off-tumor toxicity depends in part on which cells express the target antigen, a feature that bulk assays cannot resolve.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial mapping to identify which specific cells express the target antigens for antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) in breast cancer, addressing a gap that bulk assays cannot fill. By resolving target expression at the cellular level, the work helps explain both ADC efficacy and on-target/off-tumor toxicity, which depend on the cell types expressing the antigen. The approach provides a framework for better predicting ADC activity and safety in breast cancer.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to isolate intact multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) from the spleens of mice chronically infected with Leishmania donovani, a parasite causing visceral leishmaniasis. Using transcriptomic profiling of these cells, they characterize the gene expression signature of heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs, which are thought to contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. This provides the first in vivo molecular characterization of these poorly understood cells in an infectious disease context.

papers.title: Spatial Atlas of Small Cell Lung Carcinoma Reveals Intratumoral Tumor-State Heterogeneity and an MMP12+ Macrophage Niche.
papers.abstract: Small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) is a highly aggressive tumor with a dismal prognosis among lung cancers. Treatment is failing because of primary or rapidly developing secondary resistance. Recent molecular studies have suggested four SCLC subtypes with unique therapeutic vulnerabilities-ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, and YAP. These subtypes still distinguish themselves by considerable intra-tumoral heterogeneity and the influence of the microenvironmental context, which are both considered to be responsible for treatment resistance. We integrated in situ hybridization-based spatial transcriptomics w
papers.summary: This study used spatial transcriptomics to map small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC), revealing that tumors contain heterogeneous mixtures of the four known molecular subtypes (ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, YAP) within the same tumor rather than belonging to a single subtype. The authors also identified a distinct niche of MMP12+ macrophages associated with specific tumor states, highlighting how the tumor microenvironment contributes to SCLC heterogeneity and likely treatment resistance.

papers.title: A renal cyst-clear cell renal cell carcinoma comorbidity analysis identifies a FOXM1-positive epithelial COL6A1-CD44 axis that remodels fibroblasts.
papers.abstract: Renal cystic conditions are heterogeneous. We used a broad renal cyst-associated disease-gene framework to identify molecular programs shared with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), without modeling a specific cystic disorder or direct cyst-to-cancer progression.
papers.summary: The authors used a broad set of renal cyst-associated disease genes to identify molecular programs shared with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), without modeling a specific cystic disorder or direct cyst-to-cancer progression. They identify a FOXM1-positive epithelial program involving a COL6A1-CD44 axis that remodels fibroblasts, suggesting a comorbidity-linked mechanism between cystic kidney conditions and ccRCC.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to build a compact risk score for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma, centered on a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated program. The score stratifies patients by relapse risk and links it to reduced immune activity and specific single-cell expression programs.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics uncovers an invasive-desmoplastic cellular community with prognostic and therapeutic implications in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a dense desmoplastic stroma and profound spatial heterogeneity, yet the multicellular organizational principles governing its tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; n = 9) and spatial transcriptomics (n = 4), integrating 61,234 single cells and 30,430 spots to identify an invasive-frontier myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast (IF-myCAF), which is characterized by elevated expression of ACTA2, TAGLN, COL11A1, THBS2, CTHRC1, and POSTN. IF-myCAFs were validated i
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular organization of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, identifying a distinct myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast population at the tumor's invasive frontier. These IF-myCAFs, marked by genes such as ACTA2, COL11A1, and POSTN, form a multicellular community with invasive tumor cells and desmoplastic stroma that correlates with prognosis and suggests new therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics elucidates trajectories associated with transformation in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.
papers.abstract: Tumor invasion and malignant transformation are spatiotemporally coordinated processes that shape clinical behavior, diagnostic classification, and treatment response. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) are aggressive tumors that can arise sporadically or in people with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF-1) yet how distinct spatial niches underlie MPNST intra-tumor heterogeneity, local invasion or malignant transformation from benign precursors are not fully understood.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular neighborhoods within malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs), an aggressive cancer that can arise from benign precursors in neurofibromatosis type 1. By profiling gene expression while preserving tissue location, the authors identify spatial niches and transcriptional trajectories that accompany the transition from benign nerve sheath tumors to malignancy and local invasion. The work provides a spatially resolved framework for understanding MPNST heterogeneity and transformation.

papers.title: Single-cell, spatial, and machine learning analyses identify ANKIB1 as an oligodendrocyte-anchored palmitoylation-associated candidate biomarker of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive neurodegeneration and cognitive decline, yet most candidate therapies targeting amyloid-β have failed to robustly modify disease progression, underscoring an incomplete mechanistic understanding. Oligodendrocytes (ODCs) have recently emerged as active contributors to AD pathology, but the cell-type-specific role of protein S-palmitoylation - a reversible lipid post-translational modification regulating membrane targeting and trafficking - in AD remains uncharacterized. Here we performed an integrated multi-omics analysis combining single
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with machine learning to identify ANKIB1 as an oligodendrocyte-specific, palmitoylation-associated candidate biomarker for Alzheimer's disease. The work highlights oligodendrocytes as active contributors to AD pathology and links protein S-palmitoylation—a reversible lipid modification affecting membrane trafficking—to AD mechanisms in a cell-type-specific manner. ANKIB1 emerges as a potential biomarker warranting further validation.

papers.title: TRIM29 may facilitate progression of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma through immune remodeling.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy characterized by late diagnosis, aggressive progression, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Biomarkers with both diagnostic value and biological relevance remain urgently needed.
papers.journal: Pancreatology : official journal of the International Association of Pancreatology (IAP) ... [et al.]
papers.summary: This study investigates TRIM29 as a potential biomarker in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), proposing that it may promote tumor progression by remodeling the immune microenvironment. The work links TRIM29 expression to immunosuppressive features of PDAC, suggesting a role beyond simple diagnosis. However, the abstract provides limited detail on the specific mechanisms or clinical validation.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of macroregenerative and high-grade dysplastic nodules in cirrhotic liver: A pilot study.
papers.abstract: High-grade dysplastic nodules (HGDN) are recognized precursors of hepatocellular carcinoma in cirrhosis, yet their distinction from macro-regenerative nodules (MRN) relies entirely on morphologic features that exist along a continuum rather than as discrete thresholds, with no ancillary marker available to adjudicate this boundary. Whether these lesions represent distinct molecular states remains unknown. We performed whole-transcriptome spatial profiling (GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler, Bruker) of MRN and HGDN within their native cirrhotic microenvironment in FFPE explant specimens from three
papers.summary: This pilot study used spatial transcriptomic profiling to compare macroregenerative nodules and high-grade dysplastic nodules within cirrhotic liver tissue, aiming to determine whether these morphologically defined lesions represent distinct molecular states. The work addresses a diagnostic gap where no ancillary marker currently exists to distinguish these precursor lesions to hepatocellular carcinoma.

papers.title: CABOPRE: Evaluating Perioperative Cabozantinib's Efficacy and Biomarkers for Cytoreductive Nephrectomy in Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Despite advances in metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), long-term survival is poor and biomarkers are lacking. Optimal integration of cytoreductive nephrectomy (CN) in the current era remains controversial. CABOPRE, the first phase II trial assessing perioperative cabozantinib in mRCC patients eligible for CN, aimed to determine its effects in this setting, integrating tumor outcomes with molecular profiling.
papers.summary: CABOPRE is the first phase II trial testing perioperative cabozantinib in metastatic renal cell carcinoma patients undergoing cytoreductive nephrectomy. The study aims to assess efficacy and integrate tumor outcomes with molecular profiling to identify biomarkers, addressing the controversial role of cytoreductive nephrectomy in the current treatment era.

papers.title: NoiBic: a noise-tolerant biclustering algorithm for high-throughput gene expression data analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic technologies generate large-scale gene expression datasets for functional module discovery. However, technical and biological noise can obscure coherent expression patterns and compromise module detection. Noise-tolerant methods are therefore needed to recover meaningful biclusters.
papers.summary: The paper introduces NoiBic, a biclustering algorithm designed to tolerate noise in high-throughput gene expression data. It aims to recover coherent gene-condition modules that would otherwise be obscured by technical and biological noise, improving functional module discovery from transcriptomic datasets.

papers.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing single-cell expression through the lens of topic modeling.
papers.abstract: Gene-expression programs (GEPs) are the co-regulated gene modules whose coordinated activity encodes biological processes. Recovering them from single-cell RNA-seq is hard because regulation is many-to-many. A cell can run several programs at once, and a gene can take part in several. Methods that resolve programs along a trajectory break this structure by assigning each gene to a single program.
papers.summary: PRISM-GEP introduces a topic-modeling approach to recover gene-expression programs (co-regulated gene modules) from single-cell RNA-seq data without forcing each gene into a single program. This handles the many-to-many nature of gene regulation, where cells run multiple programs simultaneously and genes participate in several, unlike trajectory-based methods that break this structure. The tool offers a new lens for interpreting single-cell expression through overlapping, multi-membership programs.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activi
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from public repositories to characterize cell adhesion-related gene expression patterns in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors used Seurat-based single-cell analysis to identify cell-type-specific adhesion gene signatures, which they cross-referenced with bulk transcriptomic changes. The work nominates cell adhesion genes as candidate therapeutic targets for limiting inflammatory infiltration and preserving blood-brain barrier integrity after stroke.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to characterize the ovarian cancer microenvironment, identifying chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets as key drivers of poor clinical outcomes. The findings highlight how residual fibroblast-enriched disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy contributes to adverse prognosis, suggesting potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a transcriptomic aging clock trained with a novel 'age-shift' learning framework that predicts biological age from diverse RNA data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq and microarray, across multiple tissues. Pasta's predictions aligned with senescence and stem-like states, and the work maps chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation. This provides a versatile, platform-independent tool for studying aging biology.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are being applied to cancer epigenetics to study how local tissue context influences regulatory programs in tumors. It argues that while bulk and single-cell sequencing have advanced tumor biology, they lose spatial architecture, and spatial methods are needed to capture microenvironmental organization and cell-cell communication. The paper highlights the growing integration of spatial technologies with epigenetic analysis in cancer research.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue for immunohistochemistry, allowing them to map the development of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye on a unified timeline. They combined this with expression analysis of pigmentation and retinal markers and reanalysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data to build a developmental atlas of pigmented ocular tissues.

papers.title: Condition-Associated Pattern Extraction and Recovery From Multi-Condition Single-Cell RNA-seq Data With CAPER.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in multi-condition single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis is the disentanglement of true biological signals from unwanted variations in complex experimental designs. Current statistical and machine learning-based methods struggle with this task, often providing only visualizable embeddings, over-correcting and discarding biological signal, or failing to resolve cell-type-specific responses. Here, we present CAPER, a matrix factorization framework that explicitly disentangles shared biological states from condition-specific variations. CAPER directly outputs an
papers.summary: CAPER is a new matrix factorization framework for multi-condition single-cell RNA-seq data that separates shared biological states from condition-specific variation, addressing the tendency of existing methods to over-correct and erase real signal or to fail at resolving cell-type-specific responses. It directly outputs interpretable condition-associated patterns rather than only visual embeddings, making it easier to recover the biological signal of interest across complex experimental designs.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 computational pipelines (5 normalization methods × 4 clustering algorithms) across three cancer scRNA-seq datasets totaling over 434,000 cells, and introduces a Biological Discordance Score to quantify how marker gene interpretation shifts between pipelines. The key finding is that normalization method choice affects biological interpretation more than clustering algorithm choice, meaning pipeline decisions can materially change conclusions drawn from cancer scRNA-seq studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This study investigates how gut microbes may migrate to and influence intervertebral disc degeneration, a major cause of low back pain. It aims to identify specific microbial species and molecular mechanisms involved in the gut-disc axis, though the abstract does not yet report concrete findings.

papers.title: Spatial and Single-Cell Multi-Omics Analyses of T-Cell Subsets and Interactions in Melanoma Lymph Node Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly immunogenic malignancy, yet responses to systemic therapy remain variable. The tumour-draining lymph node (TDLN), including the sentinel lymph node (SLN) during early regional spread, is not only a site of metastatic dissemination but also an important setting for T-cell priming and immune regulation. Conventional classification of nodes as tumour-positive or tumour-negative provides essential staging information but reveals little about their immune state. Single-cell immune transcriptomics, T-cell receptor sequencing and single-cell epigenomics now allow T-cell states, c
papers.summary: This study uses spatial and single-cell multi-omics (transcriptomics, TCR sequencing, and epigenomics) to characterize T-cell subsets and their interactions in melanoma lymph node metastases. The work moves beyond the binary tumor-positive/negative staging to reveal immune states within tumor-draining lymph nodes, which are key sites for T-cell priming and immune regulation. It aims to provide a more detailed picture of the immune microenvironment that may explain variable responses to systemic therapy.

papers.title: Multi-omics integration and machine learning identify an ACKR1+ endothelial cell-based lactate-immune signature associated with carotid plaque vulnerability and progression.
papers.abstract: Early identification of vulnerable carotid plaques is crucial for stroke prevention, but the upstream metabolic processes linked to endothelial transition and immune recruitment remain poorly defined. We characterised lactate metabolism in ACKR1+ endothelial cells (ECs) in human carotid plaques and derived a machine-learning signature for discriminating plaque vulnerability.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to characterize lactate metabolism in ACKR1+ endothelial cells within human carotid plaques. The authors derive a lactate-immune signature that can discriminate vulnerable from stable plaques, potentially aiding stroke risk stratification. The work links endothelial metabolic reprogramming to immune recruitment in plaque progression.

papers.title: Integrated scRNA-Seq and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal CHPF and GPC1 as Markers of Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Dominant Domains in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in the colorectal cancer (CRC) tumor microenvironment (TME) is closely related to stromal organization and may influence treatment-related features. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic data from CRC tissues to examine cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-dominant spatial domains. GPC1 and CHPF were enriched in stromal regions and showed higher expression in CRC tissues than in normal tissues. In the analyzed cohorts, higher GPC1 and CHPF expression was associated with advanced clinicopathological features and poorer survival ou
papers.summary: By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of colorectal cancer tissues, the authors identified CHPF and GPC1 as genes enriched in cancer-associated fibroblast-dominant stromal spatial domains. Both genes were overexpressed in tumor versus normal tissue and associated with advanced clinicopathological features and worse survival. These markers may help characterize stromal heterogeneity in the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics profiling across tissue boundaries in the developing mouse brain.
papers.abstract: Tissue boundaries preserve structural integrity and guide cell differentiation during development, despite constant stress from proliferation, cell death, and tissue deformation. To study gene regulation in these regions we developed REBOSEP, a workflow for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data to detect tissue boundaries and measure gene expression relative to boundary distance. REBOSEP uses hierarchical clustering to uncover shared regulatory patterns among genes, revealing highly diverse expression changes that can shift sharply across just a few cell layers. Using this approach, the study
papers.summary: The authors developed REBOSEP, a computational workflow that detects tissue boundaries in spatial transcriptomics data and measures gene expression as a function of distance from those boundaries. Applying it to the developing mouse brain, they found that gene expression changes can be highly diverse and can shift sharply across just a few cell layers near boundaries. This provides a tool for studying how spatial position relative to tissue boundaries shapes gene regulation during development.

papers.title: Patient classification using single-cell RNA-sequencing data with deep learning convolutional neural networks.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables gene expression profiling at the resolution of individual cells, revealing cellular heterogeneity that is obscured in bulk RNA-seq. While this offers a powerful lens to study disease-specific changes, leveraging scRNA-seq data for patient phenotype classification remains challenging due to limited sample numbers, cell count variability, high dimensionality, and dependence on cell-type annotations. Existing tools attempt to address these issues using probabilistic models or attention mechanisms, but face limitations in scalability, interpretability
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning convolutional neural network approach for classifying patient phenotypes directly from single-cell RNA-sequencing data. The method aims to overcome common challenges such as small sample sizes, variable cell counts, high dimensionality, and reliance on cell-type annotations, offering a potentially more scalable and interpretable alternative to existing probabilistic or attention-based tools.

papers.title: FDX1 is associated with CALR abundance and JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling in myeloproliferative neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are driven by constitutive cytokine-receptor signaling, yet the metabolic programs associated with driver genotype and inflammatory remodeling remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study examines the metabolic protein FDX1 in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), a group of blood cancers driven by abnormal cytokine signaling. The authors report that FDX1 levels correlate with the abundance of CALR, a key MPN driver protein, and with JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling. These associations suggest FDX1 may link metabolic programs to inflammatory remodeling in MPNs, though the abstract does not specify whether the relationship is causal.

papers.title: Integrative oxidative stress-disulfidptosis analysis identifies NPR3 and ZNF366 as cell-type-associated candidate markers in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Disulfidptosis is a regulated cell-death program that occurs in SLC7A11-high cells under glucose limitation, but its relationship with oxidative stress in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remains unclear. We integrated 313 oxidative stress-related genes with 24 disulfidptosis-related genes in the original TCGA-KIRC analysis. Pearson screening (|r| ≥ 0.8 and nominal two-sided P < 0.05) identified 21 disulfidptosis-oxidative stress (DOS) genes, from which three reported DOS subtypes, 63 subtype-associated genes and a four-gene score comprising ZNF366, EMCN, GRIK3 and NPR3 were derived. In
papers.summary: This study integrates oxidative stress-related and disulfidptosis-related genes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) using TCGA data, identifying 21 overlapping genes and defining three molecular subtypes. A four-gene prognostic score (ZNF366, EMCN, GRIK3, NPR3) was derived, with NPR3 and ZNF366 highlighted as cell-type-associated candidate markers. The work is exploratory and based on bulk transcriptomic correlation analysis, so the clinical utility of these markers remains to be validated.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates publicly available fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets using computational methods to identify lipidomic features associated with colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression. The analysis suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and the lipid species CE(20:4), proposing it as a potential marker of a CRC-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The findings are exploratory and based on reanalysis of existing data rather than new experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood identifies NETosis-associated programs and a stratified adaptive immune suppression pattern in severe acute pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with persistent organ failure and substantial mortality, yet the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying progression from mild acute pancreatitis to severe-spectrum disease remain incompletely defined. Early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure remains an important unmet clinical need.
papers.summary: This study integrates peripheral blood transcriptomic datasets to identify NETosis-associated gene programs and a stratified pattern of adaptive immune suppression in severe acute pancreatitis. The findings suggest that blood-based transcriptomic signatures could help distinguish patients progressing to severe disease and persistent organ failure.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a new clustering framework for large-scale scRNA-seq data that combines a fast Louvain algorithm to generate preliminary clusters with a Transformer-based self-training step to refine them. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing clustering methods when applied to very large single-cell datasets.

papers.title: Continuous spatially informed microenvironment programs show cross-cohort concordance and context-dependent spatial organization in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics resolves tissue organization in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), whereas most clinically annotated cohorts remain bulk transcriptomic datasets.
papers.summary: This study develops a method to infer continuous, spatially informed microenvironment programs from bulk transcriptomic data by leveraging spatial transcriptomics as a reference, enabling spatial organization to be reconstructed in large clinically annotated DLBCL cohorts that lack spatial data. The inferred programs show cross-cohort concordance and reveal that spatial organization of microenvironment programs is context-dependent in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies CCDC69 as a marker associated with germinal center B-cell infiltration in TNBC: development and validation.
papers.abstract: Although coiled-coil domain containing 69 (CCDC69) has been implicated in tumor biology, its role in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and immune regulation remains unclear. Bulk transcriptomic data, single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, and spatial transcriptomics were used to investigate the role of CCDC69 in TNBC. Germinal center B-cell (GCB) signatures were quantified using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), and their associations with CCDC69 expression were assessed using correlation, ROC, and logistic regression analyses. An independent external TNBC cohort (GSE58812)
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomics to show that CCDC69 expression in triple-negative breast cancer is associated with germinal center B-cell infiltration. Using correlation, ROC, and logistic regression analyses, the authors propose CCDC69 as a potential marker linked to immune cell infiltration in TNBC, with validation in an external cohort (GSE58812).

papers.title: Loss of CLIC3 in CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes is associated with immune dysfunction and poor prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most common histological subtype of lung cancer, with a dismal prognosis partly attributed to immune evasion mediated by T cell dysfunction within the tumor microenvironment. However, the molecular determinants governing CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte functional competence remain incompletely understood. Chloride intracellular channel 3 (CLIC3) has been implicated in cancer progression, but its role in T cell immunity within the LUAD TME is unknown.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of CLIC3, a chloride channel protein, in CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes within the lung adenocarcinoma tumor microenvironment. The authors find that loss of CLIC3 in these T cells is associated with immune dysfunction and poor patient prognosis, suggesting CLIC3 may be a determinant of T cell functional competence in LUAD.

papers.title: Integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with spatial analysis identifies candidate hub genes and inferred regulatory programs in atopic dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a common chronic inflammatory disorder of the skin. Despite the availability of targeted biologics like dupilumab, heterogeneous treatment responses persist, highlighting the need for reliable biomarkers and a deeper understanding of cell-type-associated molecular programs within the tissue microenvironment.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with spatial analysis to identify candidate hub genes and infer regulatory programs in atopic dermatitis skin. The approach aims to uncover cell-type-associated molecular programs within the tissue microenvironment that may explain heterogeneous responses to biologics like dupilumab. The work provides candidate biomarkers and regulatory insights for AD, though the abstract does not report specific validated findings.

papers.title: Genetic evidence and multi-omics characterization of DEHP-relevant detoxification and metabolic heterogeneity in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Human evidence linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited, and it remains unclear whether DEHP-relevant detoxification biology captures clinically meaningful HCC heterogeneity.
papers.summary: This study integrates genetic and multi-omics data to investigate whether DEHP (a common phthalate plasticizer) exposure and detoxification biology are linked to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) heterogeneity. The authors characterize DEHP-relevant detoxification pathways and metabolic variation in HCC, aiming to identify clinically meaningful subtypes or signatures. The work provides preliminary human evidence connecting DEHP exposure biology to HCC and highlights metabolic heterogeneity that may inform risk stratification.

papers.title: Cellular, chromatin-accessibility, and spatial contextualization of bulk transcriptional patterns linked to positive peritoneal cytology in endometrial cancer.
papers.abstract: Positive peritoneal cytology (PPC) identifies a clinically adverse subset of endometrial cancer, but the tumor transcriptional patterns accompanying PPC and their cellular origins remain incompletely resolved. We evaluated PPC-linked bulk RNA patterns in TCGA-UCEC and contextualized the resulting programs using independent single-cell, chromatin-accessibility, and spatial datasets.
papers.summary: This study links bulk transcriptional patterns associated with positive peritoneal cytology (PPC) in endometrial cancer to specific cell types and chromatin states using single-cell, chromatin-accessibility, and spatial data. By contextualizing TCGA-UCEC bulk RNA signatures with independent datasets, the authors identify cellular origins and regulatory programs underlying the adverse PPC phenotype. The work provides a framework for interpreting bulk tumor signatures through multi-modal single-cell and spatial reference data.

papers.title: Mitochondrial metabolic plasticity in cancer: hybrid bioenergetic states and translational targeting in surgical oncology.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial metabolism is increasingly recognized as an active determinant of tumor growth and cancer-cell adaptation rather than solely a source of cellular energy. Mitochondrial metabolism supports tumor anabolism, while mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) alterations can affect respiratory chain function, redox homeostasis, and adaptation to changing tumor environments. At the same time, tumor metabolism is heterogeneous and flexible and cannot be explained by a uniform Warburg model. Tumor cells may use glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), or hybrid glycolysis/OXPHOS states, with the re
papers.summary: This review argues that mitochondrial metabolism actively drives tumor growth and adaptation rather than merely supplying energy, with mtDNA alterations affecting respiration, redox balance, and environmental adaptation. It emphasizes that tumors adopt heterogeneous, flexible bioenergetic states—glycolysis, OXPHOS, or hybrid glycolysis/OXPHOS—that cannot be captured by a uniform Warburg model, and discusses translational targeting implications for surgical oncology.

papers.title: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and vasculogenic mimicry in tumor vascular plasticity: a comparative bibliometric analysis and mechanistic framework.
papers.abstract: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and vasculogenic mimicry (VM) are distinct forms of cellular and vascular plasticity that may contribute to tumor vascular adaptation. Although they have largely evolved as separate research fields, emerging experimental observations suggest potential convergence in their regulation by the tumor microenvironment.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis compares the research landscapes of endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and vasculogenic mimicry (VM) in tumor vascular plasticity, two largely separate fields that emerging evidence suggests may converge under tumor microenvironment regulation. The authors propose a mechanistic framework linking the two processes. The work is primarily a literature-mapping and conceptual synthesis rather than new experimental data.
